judged_text: This call passes credentialId (the credential row primary key) as refreshOAuthTokens' userId parameter, which is serialized to the sync endpoint as calcomUserId. When sync is enabled the parent application receives a credential id where the contract (and every sibling call site, which passes credential.userId) says Cal.com user id, so zoho-bigin token sync matches no user — or the wrong user where the ids numerically collide — and zoho-bigin credentials silently never refresh.

When sync is enabled the parent application receives a credential id where the contract (and every sibling call site, which passes credential.userId) says Cal.com user id, so zoho-bigin token sync matches no user — or the wrong user where the ids numerically collide — and zoho-bigin credentials silently never refresh.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the third parameter is explicitly `userId: number | null` and, when syncing is enabled, it is serialized as `calcomUserId` in the POST body. In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call site passes `credentialId` as that third argument (`refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`), while other updated call sites consistently pass `credential.userId`. This mismaps the contract and would send a credential row id to the sync endpoint instead of the Cal.com user id, causing refresh/token sync to fail or target the wrong user if ids collide.
